bull.b: Early clinical evidence supports the lead program: all five low-dose participants showed meaningful improvement in at least one visual-function measure, while four had structural gains. The favorable safety profile strengthens the program’s basis for continued development in inherited retinal disease.

FDA alignment on a potential pivotal microperimetry endpoint, together with agreement on Phase 3 and commercial manufacturing requirements, creates a clearer development route. This supports a defined transition toward pivotal testing and planned 2027 dosing for OPGx-BEST1.

An updated U.S. estimate of 23,600 BEST1 patients expands the apparent addressable population, while Cohort 2 was over-enrolled. Together, these signals support a broader potential commercial opportunity and continued clinical interest as OPGx-BEST1 advances.

bear.b: TTM net margin of about -1,092% and EBIT/EBITDA margins around -1,065% show that current revenue is far from covering the operating cost base. Persistent heavy losses reduce internal funding capacity and increase reliance on future financing or commercial progress.

TTM operating and free cash flow were both about -$53.4M, worsening from roughly -$35.3M in 2025, with negative cash flow since 2023. This sustained burn consumes resources needed for development and increases dependence on external capital.

TTM stockholders’ equity fell to about -$13.0M while total debt reached roughly $34.9M, versus no debt and positive equity during 2023–2025. This reversal weakens financial flexibility and can constrain funding choices while losses continue.
